property_summary: For any caller who is the owner and any positive contract balance, calling withdrawAll() transfers the entire contract balance to the owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant that withdraws only half breaks this by leaving a nonzero balance for some inputs.

For any owner who calls withdrawAll when the contract has an arbitrary nonzero balance, the correct contract drains the entire contract balance to the owner (address(c).balance == 0 afterwards); the mutant that withdraws only half leaves a nonzero balance for some fuzzed deposit amount and thus violates this rule.

For any caller who is the owner and any nonzero contract balance funded via fallback, calling withdrawAll drains the contract to zero balance; the mutant that withdraws only half will leave a nonzero balance for some fuzzed deposit amounts, breaking this rule.

If the owner calls withdrawAll when the contract balance is odd or even, the correct contract forwards the entire balance to the owner (so address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant that only withdraws half will leave a nonzero balance for some fuzzed deposit amounts — we express this by first funding the contract with a fuzzed amount via fallback and asserting address(c).balance == 0 after owner's withdrawAll.

For any owner who calls withdrawAll after funding the contract by sending any positive amount from that owner, the reference contract will transfer the entire contract balance to the owner (leaving address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that uses half the balance will leave a nonzero contract balance for some fuzzed funding amounts, violating this rule.

Invariant: Only the contract owner can successfully withdraw the contract's balance via withdrawAll (so address(c).balance becomes 0 only when called by the owner); the mutant removing the onlyOwner check allows non-owners to drain the contract, violating this rule for some caller addresses and balances.

For any recipient address and any withdraw amount <= contract balance, the reference contract's withdraw never silently fail — transfer either sends the funds or reverts, so a call to withdraw always results in the contract's balance decreasing by the requested amount (or reverts); the mutant using send can silently fail when the recipient is a contract whose fallback/receive reverts, leaving contract balance unchanged.

For any recipient contract and any withdraw amount that the owner asks to withdraw, the correct contract's withdraw always reverts if the recipient's receive/fallback reverts (so the call does not silently leave funds in the contract), while the mutant using send can return false and leave the contract balance unchanged — i.e., for all inputs the reference makes withdraw either succeed and reduce address(c).balance by amount or revert, whereas the mutant can return false (no revert) leaving address(c).balance unchanged.

For every caller (owner) and every target contract with a failing receive/fallback, the reference's withdraw will revert (so the call does not complete successfully), whereas the mutant using send can return false and therefore complete without reverting — so the universal rule: calling withdraw on a target whose fallback/receive ALWAYS reverts must never complete successfully on the reference (it must revert); the mutant sometimes completes successfully (returns) and thus violates this.

For any owner and any recipient contract that REVERTS on receiving ether, calling withdraw(...) from the owner always reverts on the reference (because transfer bubbles the revert), whereas the mutant using send can return false and NOT revert, allowing the call to complete — so the reference's withdraw never returns successfully when the recipient reverts but the mutant sometimes does.

For every owner-initiated withdraw(amount) where the recipient contract's fallback consumes more than 2300 gas (by performing a state write), the reference (using transfer) will revert (preventing the withdraw from returning successfully), while the mutant (using send) may return false and allow withdraw to complete without sending funds — so the reference never completes successfully against a gas-consuming recipient, but the mutant can.

For any caller and any amount, only the contract owner can successfully withdraw funds from the contract; the mutant that removes onlyOwner allows non-owners to withdraw causing address(c).balance to drop when called by non-owner.

For every caller and every amount, only the contract owner can successfully withdraw funds from the contract (non-owners cannot reduce address(c).balance by calling withdraw); the mutant removing onlyOwner allows a non-owner to withdraw and thus can reduce address(c).balance for some inputs.

For every caller and value, the reference contract only allows the owner to successfully withdraw (calls to withdraw by owner succeed and change contract balance accordingly while non-owners revert), whereas the mutant inverts the check and thus allows non-owners to withdraw (and/or causes owner calls to fail) for some inputs.

For every caller and value, only the contract deployer (owner) can successfully call withdraw and cause the contract balance to decrease by that value; the mutant inverts the check and therefore allows a non-owner caller to withdraw (or prevents the owner), so there exists some caller/value where behavior differs.

For every target address and amount, the reference contract's sendMoney reverts when the low-level call to the target fails (i.e., it only returns successfully if the external call succeeded), but the mutant that removes the require allows sendMoney to succeed even if the external call failed.

For any target address that reverts when receiving funds, the reference contract's sendMoney returns a failed low-level call (observable as the call completing without reverting and leaving contract balance unchanged) while the mutant using transfer will revert the sendMoney call; thus the reference never reverts for such failing callees but the mutant sometimes does.

For any target contract that rejects/consumes Ether on receive, the reference C will not revert when sendMoney is called (it returns false from the low-level call and leaves C's balance unchanged), whereas the mutant using transfer will revert the call; thus for all admissible inputs the reference never reverts but the mutant reverts for some inputs.

For any target address that is a contract which deliberately uses more than 2300 gas in its receive/fallback (so a transfer would fail), the reference C's sendMoney never reverts (it returns/continues because it uses low-level call and checks the boolean), while the mutant using transfer will revert; therefore for all admissible inputs the reference's sendMoney call completes (ok == true) but the mutant can cause it to revert (ok == false) for some fuzzed value of _value and attacker contract address.
